header:
Problem 9 Skeletal Reconstruction of Alkaloids
Late-stage skeletal modification and precise remodeling of natural products provide an ideal shortcut for rapidly expanding compound libraries and discovering breakthrough drugs. In 2026, Amir H. Hoveyda's team reported an isolable, general-purpose platform generated by Hofmann elimination (HE), followed by a general strategy for divergent construction of new nonnatural frameworks through rearrangement, ring-closing metathesis, or intramolecular hydroamination.

subquestions.text_open: 9.1.1 Under specific conditions, anhydrovinblastine reacts with a chlorine source to introduce a chlorine atom and form electrically neutral intermediate A1. In the presence of $AgBF_4$ and solvent, intramolecular reorganization occurs through intermediates A2 and A3, ultimately giving vinorelbine, a widely used clinical anticancer drug. Write the SMILES strings for the key intermediates A1, A2, and A3.

The chlorine source is also drawn above the arrow and has SMILES 'CN1C2=CC=CC=C2N=N1.[Cl]'. R is the original placeholder in the figure.

subquestions.text_open: 9.1.2 Under further basic conditions, nucleophilic conjugate addition introduces an alkynyl aldehyde fragment into vinorelbine to give A4. C-N bond cleavage then forms A5, followed by cyclization and desilylation to afford a two-carbon ring-expanded analogue. Write the SMILES strings for the two key intermediates A4 and A5.

subquestions.text_open:
9.2 While studying skeletal deconstruction of vinpocetine, the researchers encountered an unexpected product. Reaction of vinpocetine with 5.0 equivalents of allyl iodide efficiently formed a quaternary ammonium salt. Subsequent treatment in potassium ethoxide/ethanol (KOEt/EtOH) at 80°C for 2 h gave not only the expected ring-opened product in 58% yield but also a deallylated secondary-amine byproduct in 32% yield, as shown. Isotopic-labeling experiments demonstrated that formation of the byproduct did not arise from direct $S_N2$ allylic nucleophilic substitution, but proceeded through a rapid and reversible acid-base proton-exchange process.
9.2.1 Write the SMILES string for the key enammonium cation intermediate B formed after deprotonation of the quaternary ammonium salt and used to explain the deallylated byproduct.

text_images.description: The figure shows a two-step reaction: '[R]C1=C[C@]2(CC)CCCN([C@@H]23)CCC4=C3N1C5=CC=CC=C45'>5.0 equiv. allyl iodide, MeCN, 3 h, 80 °C>'[R]C1=C[C@@]2(CCC[N@@+]3(CCC4=C([C@H]23)N1C5=CC=CC=C45)C(C=C)[H])CC.[I-]'; '[R]C1=C[C@@]2(CCC[N@@+]3(CCC4=C([C@H]23)N1C5=CC=CC=C45)C(C=C)[H])CC.[I-]'>KOEt, EtOH, + aq. workup>'[R]C(N1C2=C(C(C=C)=C1[C@H]3NCCC4)C=CC=C2)=C[C@@]34CC'. R is the original placeholder in the figure.

subquestions.text_open:
9.2.2 If the KOEt/EtOH system above is replaced by the deuterated reagent system KOEt/EtOD and the vincane-derived quaternary ammonium salt is treated at 80°C, partially deuterated products are obtained. Quantitative nuclear magnetic resonance ($^1H$ NMR) analysis shows unequal deuteration at the allylic positions of the recovered diene substrate: 33% at $H^b$ and 16% at $H^c$. At the most acidic benzylic proton $H^a$, no appreciable deuteration is observed because elimination is too rapid.
Write the SMILES string for intermediate C in this kinetic proton-exchange process.

text_images.description: Organic reaction scheme: '[R]C1=C[C@@]2(CCC[N@@+]3(CCC4=C([C@H]23)N1C5=CC=CC=C45)[C@@H](/C=C/[Hc])[Hb])CC.[I-]'>KOEt, EtOD>'[R]C1=C[C@@]2(CCC[N@@+]3(CCC4=C([C@H]23)N1C5=CC=CC=C45)[C@@H](/C=C/[Dc])[Db])CC.[I-]'. R is the original placeholder, and [Hb], [Hc], [Db], and [Dc] are the original hydrogen/deuterium labels in the figure.

subquestions.text_open:
9.3 When the proton environment of the reaction is changed, a reactive carbanion intermediate can be directed onto an entirely different rearrangement pathway.
9.3.1 Vincane is reacted with allyl iodide to form intermediate D, which is then treated with KOEt in anhydrous acetonitrile. Rather than undergoing elimination, it gives a C-allylated product in 65% yield with exceptionally high asymmetric stereoselectivity of >98:2 d.r.
Give the specific name of the concerted rearrangement in this step, and write the SMILES string for intermediate D with the stereochemistry of its stereogenic centers shown explicitly.

text_images.description: The figure shows a two-step reaction: 'CC[C@]12CCCN3CCC4=C([C@@H]23)N(CC1)C5=CC=CC=C45'>2.0 equiv. allyl iodide, MeCN>[D]; [D]>3.0 equiv. KOEt, (no EtOH), 1 h, 22 °C>'C=CC[C@]12C(N(CC3)C4=CC=CC=C54)=C5CCN1CCC[C@@]32CC'.

subquestions.text_open: 9.3.2 The product from the previous step reacts with MeOTf to form quaternary ammonium salt E, which is again treated with strong base for elimination. DFT calculations show that, to relieve steric compression, a particular C-N bond in E is substantially elongated to 1.61 Å and is therefore highly susceptible to cleavage. Elimination ultimately occurs selectively at the less accessible but more acidic C-H bond, giving the ten-membered-ring exo-bridged diene F. Write the SMILES strings for quaternary ammonium salt E and elimination product F.

text_images.description: The figure shows a two-step reaction: 'C=CC[C@]12C(N(CC3)C4=CC=CC=C54)=C5CCN1CCC[C@@]32CC'>3.0 equiv. MeOTf, DCE, 16 h, 70 °C>[E]; [E]>3.0 equiv. KOEt, EtOH, 3 h, 80 °C>[F]. E and F are shown only as labels; their structures are not drawn.

subquestions.text_open:
9.4 While attempting ring-closing metathesis (RCM) of an oxidized tetrahydropalmatine derivative to construct a medium-sized oxygen-containing ring, the research team encountered an unusual reverse process. When the Lewis acid $BPh_3$ was added to the W catalyst, the reaction did not give the expected ten-membered-ring metathesis product. Instead, it afforded a ring-contracted isomer bearing a stereogenic vinyl substituent in 61% yield.
A Lewis acid-base adduct forms first, followed by an extremely rare reverse Meisenheimer rearrangement (RMR) to give boron-complex intermediate G. Write the SMILES strings for G and the boron-containing organic byproduct formed with the product.

subquestions.text_open:
9.5 While attempting to isomerize the double bonds of the substrate above, the researchers found that treatment in a $KO^tBu$/DMSO system at room temperature (22°C) gave quantitative conversion in only 30 min, with >98% yield, to an aryl-substituted dehydroisoquinoline derivative. In subsequent biological-activity tests, this molecule showed remarkably potent anticancer activity at nanomolar concentrations.
Theoretical calculations (DFT) and deuterium-control experiments showed that rapid elimination first forms the $(DMSO)_3K^+$-associated π-allyl-type conjugated complex intermediate $H_1$. With assistance from the potassium ion, this intermediate then undergoes a thermodynamically highly favorable anionic [1,6]-hydrogen proton-transfer process, an 8-electron pericyclic reaction with an activation barrier of only 15.9 kcal/mol, to form $H_2$. Write the SMILES strings for intermediates $H_1$ and $H_2$.
